user_prompt:
[Image: A person looking at a solid made of cubes]

The solid is made of 5 small cubes.
Which shape does the person in the diagram see?

Figure, described in words:
At the top of the item, a person is standing to the left of a three-dimensional solid made of 5 small identical cubes. The person is shown in side profile facing right toward the solid, with a horizontal dotted line extending from the person's eyes to the top-left cube of the solid. The solid is drawn in isometric projection and consists of:
- A central vertical column of 3 cubes.
- One cube attached to the back-right of the top cube of the column, at the same height as the top cube.
- One cube attached to the front-right of the middle cube of the column, extending forward toward the viewer at the middle height level.

The response options each show a flat 2D shape composed of connected unit squares:
- Option A: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square.
- Option B: 4 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.
- Option C: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the middle square and 1 square attached to the right of the top square.
- Option D: 5 squares consisting of a vertical column of 3 squares with 1 square attached to the left of the top square and 1 square attached to the right of the middle square.

A. [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the middle square]
B. [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the right of the middle square]
C. [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the middle square and one square attached to the right of the top square]
D. [Image: A vertical column of three squares with one square attached to the left of the top square and one square attached to the right of the middle square]

llm_thinking:
I'm figuring out the view from the left side, trying to assign coordinates to each cube in the solid to determine which squares would be visible—narrowing options down to those showing four squares, then working out the exact positions of the column and attached cubes.

This is tricky to pin down geometrically — I suspect the front-right cube on the middle one ends up hidden behind the column when viewed from the left, since it extends toward the picture's original viewer rather than toward this new vantage point. That would leave a column of three squares plus the back-right cube on top poking out to one side, giving four visible squares total, though I need to check which side it lands on to match the answer choices.

Since person's left corresponds to back (+y) and the back cube is at top, that square goes on the left of top; the front cube at middle maps to the right side for the person. That matches option D, so I'll go with D.
